notes: Odo's book of makings (training level B2, D-59): a readable thing, like the wainwright's notebook. Advice in the world, not a recipe system: every attempt is still judged and nothing is keyed to these words. 'need' names things as they lie in the workshop; 'say' is a sentence the reader can send with Type it for me.
title: Odo's Book of Makings
intro: Odo Tinker, his book. If you can read this, you can help.

Most things that break can be mended, and most things you need can be made from what's lying about. Look at what a thing is made of before you start: flax twists, leather bends, pitch burns and sticks.
The world decides whether it works. If it doesn't, it'll tell you why.

recipes.name: Flax rope
steps: Twist each strand the same way, tight.
Lay the three together and twist them back the other way: the rope holds itself.
recipes.say: twist the flax fibres into a rope
recipes.good_for: Tying, hauling, hanging a bucket. Rots if left wet.

recipes.name: Pitch torch
steps: Wind the rag tight round one end of the stick.
Tie it off so it won't slip.
Dip the wrapped end in the pitch and let it soak.
recipes.say: wind the linen rag round the end of the ash stick and soak it in the pine pitch to make a torch
recipes.good_for: Light in the dark; burns for half an hour. Light it at a fire.

recipes.name: Leather sling
steps: Cut a pouch from the middle of the leather strip.
Tie a length of twine to each end of the pouch.
Loop one cord round your finger; let the other go as you swing.
recipes.say: make a sling from the strip of leather and the hemp twine
recipes.good_for: Throwing stones a long way. Takes practice.
